text:
READY TO IMPLEMENT THE MEMBERSHIP ROUTING AND STOPPING ON ONE QUESTION, because the answer decides
WHICH SIX FIGURES MOVE AND BY HOW MUCH, and I would be inventing it rather than deriving it.

Your ruling was direction, and it is unambiguous: resolved-but-unconcentrated mass goes into
PlacementResolution's `excluded` arm, attributed, so a unit publishable by resolution while
belonging to no class stops clearing the threshold and the conditional metrics abstain. The carrier
landed at 1fa3c51 - ExclusionCause.BelowMembership carries the threshold, excludedBy sums and
absorbs, everything is guarded.

WHAT I CANNOT DERIVE IS THE PREDICATE. Your example is "a unit resolved at 0.6 while a member of no
class at 0.3 each". Read against the source, "member of a class" is not one notion:

  Scoring.scala:384  private val MembershipThreshold = 0.5
  Scoring.scala:413  as.exists(a => phasePred(...) && a.targetMass >= MembershipThreshold)
  Scoring.scala:502  as.exists(_.massAt(pred) >= MembershipThreshold)     <- pred varies per metric
  Scoring.scala:564  assessments.filter(_.targetMass >= MembershipThreshold)

So membership is evaluated PER METRIC with a different predicate each time. There is no single "the
unit reached no class" fact in the model today - there are as many facts as there are predicates,
and a unit can be a member under one and not another.

THE THREE READINGS, and they move different numbers:
  (A) TARGET ONLY - unconcentrated means targetMass < 0.5. Narrowest, matches :413 and :564, and is
      the notion the traditional sheet already uses. Moves the target-dependent metrics.
  (B) NO PREDICATE REACHED - excluded iff the assessment reaches NO metric's predicate at 0.5.
      Closest to your sentence's plain meaning, and the strictest: mass is excluded only when it
      classifies nowhere at all.
  (C) PER-METRIC - each metric excludes the mass unconcentrated for ITS OWN predicate, so one
      detail can be excluded from eventPurity and resolved for semanticization. Most faithful to how
      the metrics actually work, and it means PlacementResolution is no longer ONE summary per
      account - it becomes one per metric, which is a much larger change than the carrier.

I lean (B): it keeps a single resolution summary per account, it is what "belongs to nothing being
measured" says, and it is conservative - it only excludes mass that no metric could have used. But
(C) is arguably the truthful one and it is a bigger design than the ruling contemplated, so I am not
going to pick it silently.

I HAVE NOT WRITTEN ANY OF IT. Files reserved under rv-01M19G7E8Y88E1MZ300JR671J6, nothing edited,
worktree clean. Tell me A, B or C and I will implement it with the before/after on all six figures
in the candidate, so the movement is attributable exactly as ADR 0003 requires. If you would rather
this wait behind the supportWeight work on bd-01M19956MFSG7076QE4J66T7E9 - since both are about what
an unmeasurable quantity should publish - that is also a reasonable answer and I will release the
reservation.
